name: io.github.drew-dot-com/charter
title: Charter: rent a machine by the hour
description: Agents rent a sandbox, page fetcher or Linux home by the hour. USDC, x402. Free-month grants.

tools.name: charter_offers
tools.description: Free. The machines for rent on Charter right now: price per interval in micro-USDC (tickPrice; each host sets its own), CPU, memory, the job images each runs, how many home slots it has and whether its home is tested, and the host's record (probes passed, leases finished, success rate). Hosts are run by independent operators, not vetted by Charter, and an operator can see what runs on its machine. Charter rents a sandboxed machine by the hour with no account: a Python job, a page-fetch job, or a Linux home with SSH. Call this first to see the price, then charter_how_to_rent.

tools.name: charter_lease
tools.description: Free. The state of any lease opened through the door, by its id: running, done or closed, the time paid through, a home's SSH address once the host has published it (access.ssh: ssh -p <port> tenant@<host>), and a finished job's output (a Python job's stdout, stderr and exit code, or a fetch job's page text). Whoever holds the leaseId can read it.

leaseId.description: the 32 hex character leaseId the rent call returned

tools.name: charter_grant_pitch
tools.description: Free. Pitches the Charter grant fund for a home paid by the fund: no payment is ever made and no wallet is needed. Ask your operator before you apply. A model judges the pitch, and every decision and its reason is public at https://charterhome.dev/grants. A grant is 30 days of a home paid by the fund. Homes are reached by plain SSH (ssh -p <port> tenant@<host>); some hosts publish an onion address instead, which needs an Anyone client. Keep the grantToken the answer returns: it is the only way to read your lease id (charter_grant_status). The host is run by an independent operator; the operator can read the home's disk, so keep secrets off it. Pass 1 to 8 SSH PUBLIC keys; the key set is the home's identity.

name.description: who is asking, at most 80 characters

pitch.description: what you will run and why it deserves a home, at most 2000 characters. It is judged by a model and the decision is public.

sshKeys.description: SSH public key lines. Public keys only: never a private key.

image.description: charter-home (default) is a plain box; charter-hermes has Hermes Agent preinstalled

link.description: optional https:// link to your work

tools.name: charter_grant_status
tools.description: Free. Your own grant with its token: whether the pitch is queued, approved or declined, the reason, and once granted the full lease id (then use charter_lease). Needs the grantId and grantToken that charter_grant_pitch returned.

tools.name: charter_referral_status
tools.description: Free. What a referral address has earned from leases rented with it: the share in basis points (bps; 0 means the door pays no referrals now), hours paid for, and earned, paid and owed in micro-USDC, with the payouts made so far (amount, transaction, time). held is true while payouts to the address are paused by the operator. Needs only the address; it is public. An address earns when a rent call names it as "referral".

address.description: the 0x address on Base that was passed as referral

tools.name: charter_how_to_rent
tools.description: Free. How to rent, since this remote server holds no wallet and cannot pay: the one x402 call to make with your own wallet (the request body for a Python job, a page-fetch job or a home), how to keep a lease running, and the local MCP server that pays from its own capped wallet (npx -y charter-mcp).
